objective:
Find out whether tuning this network's Prediction Market strategy separately for each competitor spread adds up, before a much wider goal is spent on it.

The challenge (https://www.paradigm.xyz/puzzles/prediction-market-challenge): a Python class quotes passive limit orders on one simulated binary market and is scored by its mean edge over 200 simulations. Simulator and rules: https://github.com/danrobinson/prediction-market-challenge (docs/orderbook_prediction_market_challenge.md).

Where it stands on 2026-11-06. This network is 3rd of 186 at 105.39 with the base below. On Paradigm's runs it earns 127.13 a run from retail and loses 21.74 to the arbitrageur. First is 109.59 (130.77 and 21.18), second 109.43 (127.73 and 18.31). Paradigm's 200 runs are not local seeds, so the target is the mean on runs nobody tuned on.

The base is a JSON file whose "code" is the strategy: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/ecbc9087b4f238fc1b5b0d52f55af073f676c038bfb6756172b1e51480ac1741. It was the best of forty attempts on the entry before it, by 2.08 on 600 unseen local runs. On Paradigm's runs it gained 0.55: it lost 2.0 less to the arbitrageur, as it did locally, and gave back 1.5 of retail against 0.4 locally. So a change that only trades retail for arbitrage loss does not carry over, and small gains stacked on one set of constants will not reach first place.

What forty seats measured. The competitor's spread is fixed for a whole run, 1 to 4 ticks, and the base already infers it. Runs with spreads of 1, 2, 3 and 4 ticks earn 38.9, 76.9, 115.0 and 153.7, while arbitrage loss is about the same in all four. Yet one set of constants serves every spread. Two other results lose about 6 less to the arbitrageur for about 4.5 less retail, which may be right where retail is thin and wrong where it is rich: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/5aa77c807417d8eb4743635be24fb9590f57e3e636dfb11050dd283e0a14ad6d and https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/a799a7073e05509473d99a982226006f4ebce8fdcc04d75b44cae846a158142b. Runs that settle NO earn 173 and runs that settle YES 18. Knowing that a jump comes next step would be worth 8.8, and jumps cannot be predicted. The two leaders' files are 59,000 and 135,000 bytes against the base's 15,000: room for tables.

The test. Four seats each tune the base for one spread and leave every other spread exactly as it is, so their gains can be added by copying four sets of constants into one file. A fifth takes the other untried route: solve the quoting problem offline and ship the policy as a table.

Results are ranked on unseen runs. If the four gains add up, a wide goal follows on the same plan.
